title: bug: create_task writes the row before it trips on a non-array definitionOfDone (createTask.ts:197 then throws an uncoded TypeError), so the caller gets an error for a task that exists and its retry files a duplicate, and taskRails entries are stored with no type or length check (a non-string rail later crashes propose_rail)
description:
Filed by defect hunt #12 (task-f6f0b580, architect-1dd28c7c). Reproduced at moe/work-2026-10-24 f159784e; the files are unchanged at cbae6070. This is a guard gap, not a live incident.

PROBLEM (packages/moe-daemon/src/):
- create_task checks dependsOn's shape before the write (tools/createTask.ts:87-92, "shape errors throw").
- definitionOfDone is not checked.
  - state.createTask (createTask.ts:157-166) sanitizes a non-array to the placeholder ['Task completed as described'] (state/taskStore.ts:315-317) and writes the row.
  - Then createTask.ts:197 runs `params.definitionOfDone?.filter(...)` on the raw value. That throws "params.definitionOfDone?.filter is not a function", which reaches the caller as -32000 with no task id.
  - The schema says array (createTask.ts:35), but McpAdapter does not enforce schemas. The natural retry files a second row.
- taskRails: taskStore.ts:327 stores `input.taskRails.slice(0, 100)` raw, with no string check and no length cap.
  - epicRails are refused when they are not strings or exceed MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS (validateEpicUpdates, state/validators.ts:584).
  - A stored non-string rail crashes railChange.ts:12 `rail.trimEnd()` with an uncoded TypeError. That line is reached from proposeRail.ts:62 for a TASK-scope MODIFY or REMOVE.
  - get_context serves an over-long rail to every seat.

EVIDENCE (git-archive snapshot of f159784e; my re-runs are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/me/):
- /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/A/zzHuntA_createTaskDodShape.test.ts: Tests 5 failed | 1 passed (6).
  - ✓ (sibling) a malformed dependsOn is refused with INVALID_INPUT and writes nothing
  - × a plain string, a stringified JSON array and an object each → AssertionError: expected { wrote: true, threw: true, …(1) } to deeply equal { wrote: false, threw: true, …(1) }
  - × (r-msg) → expected 'TypeError: params.definitionOfDone?.f…' not to match /is not a function/
  - × (r-retry) → expected [ 'bug: x', 'bug: x' ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
- /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/A/zzHuntA_createTaskRails.test.ts: Tests 3 failed | 1 passed (4).
  - ✓ (sibling) create_epic refuses a non-string or over-long rail with INVALID_INPUT
  - × (r1) a non-string rail is stored
  - × (r2) a 200k-char rail is stored
  - × (r3) → expected 'TypeError: rail.trimEnd is not a func…' not to match /is not a function/
- Exposure:
  - Of the 956 rows, no pair shares a title, carries the placeholder DoD and was created minutes apart (the retry signature).
  - 0 of the 897 live rows that have taskRails hold a bad entry.

FIX DIRECTION: in create_task, before state.createTask:
- refuse a present definitionOfDone or taskRails that is not an array of strings, with INVALID_INPUT, as dependsOn is refused (the state-level sanitizer can stay as a backstop);
- refuse a taskRails entry longer than MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS, as create_epic does for epicRails (validateStringArrayValue may fit);
- compute dodCount from the stored task.definitionOfDone, not the raw param.
A bound placed in taskStore.createTask also covers /ws CREATE_TASK.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskStore.ts (createTask only), and a new packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.shape.test.ts. Sync `### moe.create_task` only if docs/MCP_SERVER.md is free at planning time.

Held for after this row lands, because they touch the same files:
- create_task stores `order` unchecked, and nextTaskOrder (taskStore.ts:844-848) lets one non-finite order poison every later default order. This is the task twin of 68a47060's epic fix. Repro: A/zzHuntA_createTaskOrder.test.ts. 0 live rows are affected.
- /ws CREATE_TASK stores any status (taskStore.ts:334). Repro: B/zzHuntB_createTaskStatus.test.ts. No plugin sends status.
definitionOfDone: create_task with a definitionOfDone or taskRails that is present but not an array of strings (a string, a stringified JSON array, an object, or an array holding a number) is refused INVALID_INPUT naming the field, no task file is written, and a retry with valid input creates exactly one row.
A taskRails entry longer than MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS is refused INVALID_INPUT, as create_epic refuses an over-long epicRails entry.
A new vitest file covers these cases and the valid path (array DoD and rails stored as given) and passes, and createTask.test.ts stays green.

implementationPlan.description:
Refuse a malformed definitionOfDone or taskRails before the write, and test it. File: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.ts. Do NOT edit state/taskStore.ts: this task's checks all run in the tool, and the held-back order and /ws status items own that file.
(a) Directly after the priority check (createTask.ts:80-83) and before the dependsOn block, add the checks below, with a 3-line comment saying why: a non-array DoD used to be sanitized to the placeholder and written, after which the dodCount line threw an uncoded TypeError, so the caller saw an error for a row that existed and a retry filed a duplicate.
  - definitionOfDone: if it is present and not null (`params.definitionOfDone != null`): throw invalidInput('definitionOfDone', 'must be an array of strings') when !Array.isArray, and invalidInput(`definitionOfDone[${i}]`, 'must be a string') for any non-string entry. That is the whole check. Do NOT add empty-entry, count or length refusals: sanitizeStringArray (util/sanitize.ts:123) keeps trimming empty entries, slicing to 50 items and truncating to 1000 chars, so [] and [''] still get the placeholder and the 'definitionOfDone is empty' warning.
  - taskRails: `const taskRails = params.taskRails == null ? undefined : validateStringArrayValue(params.taskRails, 'taskRails', 100, MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS, false);`. Import both from '../state/validators.js'. These are the exact bounds create_epic applies to epicRails (validators.ts:584): an array of at most 100 non-empty strings of at most 10000 chars. Pass `taskRails` (not params.taskRails) to state.createTask.
  - Type params.definitionOfDone and params.taskRails as unknown and narrow after the checks. Keep the dodCount line computing from the validated param, NOT from the stored task.definitionOfDone: the stored placeholder would hide the empty-DoD warning. This deliberately departs from the row's fix hint.
  - null on either field stays 'absent', as today, so there is no contract change for null-sending clients.
(b) New packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.shape.test.ts, using the createTask.test.ts harness (ToolTestHarness, setupMoeFolder, createEpic, state.load). Write each assertion so it fails at HEAD.
  - DoD 'Tests pass', '["a","b"]', {a:1} and ['ok', 1]: each rejects with codeName INVALID_INPUT and a message naming definitionOfDone (or definitionOfDone[1]). The task count is unchanged, no new file appears in .moe/tasks, and no TASK_CREATED is logged.
  - Retry: after a refused call, a valid call with the same title creates exactly one row with that title.
  - taskRails 'r', {}, [42], ['ok', null], [''] and 101 entries: each is INVALID_INPUT naming taskRails or taskRails[i], with nothing written.
  - taskRails 'x'.repeat(MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS + 1) is refused, and exactly MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS is accepted.
  - Valid path: DoD ['a','b','c'] and rails ['r1'] are stored exactly as given. null DoD and null rails act as absent: placeholder DoD with the empty warning, and rails [].
  - Warning guard: DoD [] and [''] still produce the 'definitionOfDone is empty' warning and the placeholder.
Move the hunt repros (/mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/A/zzHuntA_createTaskDodShape.test.ts and zzHuntA_createTaskRails.test.ts) into these cases rather than copying them verbatim.
implementationPlan.note: Pre-write DoD + taskRails shape checks; new shape test (12/19 fail without the fix).

implementationPlan.description:

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && awk '$0=="### moe.create_task"{p=1;next} p&&/^### /{exit} p' docs/MCP_SERVER.md | grep -q 'Input refusals' && S=$(mktemp -d) && git archive HEAD packages/moe-daemon | tar -x -C "$S" && cp --parents packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.ts packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/createTask.shape.test.ts "$S" && cd "$S/packages/moe-daemon" && env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin" NO_COLOR=1 sh -c 'npm ci --no-audit --no-fund >/dev/null 2>&1 && npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/tools/createTask.shape.test.ts src/tools/createTask.test.ts src/tools/createCommitActor.test.ts src/tools/epicDeleteActor.test.ts src/tools/getContext.test.ts'
The extra test files are every other test that calls createTaskTool. Red-first proof for the completion summary: revert only the createTask.ts hunk and the shape test must fail; restore it and the test passes.
implementationPlan.note: Verified in a snapshot. The plan's archive omits docs/roles, which one getContext test scans, so I archived docs/roles too. 95/95 pass, tsc clean.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of your diff (`git diff $(git merge-base HEAD "${MOE_LAND_TARGET:-HEAD}")`): expect createTask.ts, the new test and the one doc paragraph, roughly +170/-3. Error handling: check each item and fix what fails.
(1) Both checks run before state.createTask and before any await that writes. Nothing (worker record, activity, chat) is written on a refusal.
(2) null and absent behave exactly as before for both fields. [] and [''] DoD still give the placeholder and the empty warning.
(3) No uncoded TypeError remains on the dodCount line for any input shape: it only ever sees undefined, null or string[].
(4) taskRails at exactly 10000 chars and exactly 100 entries is accepted, and one more is refused. Parity with create_epic's epicRails.
(5) state.createTask receives the validated taskRails array, and the taskStore.ts slice stays a harmless backstop.
(6) Each test asserts the refusal codeName, the named field and that nothing was written (task count, files, TASK_CREATED), not merely 'it threw'.
(7) The /ws CREATE_TASK path is untouched, as is the held-back order poisoning in taskStore.nextTaskOrder. Both are named in the completion summary as out of scope.
If anything changes, re-run the step-3 command and submit that fresh output.
implementationPlan.note: Self-review items 1-7 pass; no changes after the step-3 run.

comments.content: Correction from the filer, for the planner. The description says to sync `### moe.create_task` "only if docs/MCP_SERVER.md is free at planning time". That wording is out of date. Governor ruling msg-71db57ac (21:06Z) says: include this row's own `### moe.create_task` sync as a plan step that edits only that section. Defer it only if another open row's plan edits the same section. lanes.js listing MCP_SERVER.md under another row is not a reason to skip. Document the new INVALID_INPUT refusals for a non-array definitionOfDone or taskRails and for an over-long rail.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.create_task refuses a present, non-null definitionOfDone that is not an array of strings, and a present, non-null taskRails that fails create_epic's epicRails bounds (an array of at most 100 non-empty strings, each at most MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS). Either refusal is INVALID_INPUT naming the field, raised before any write. A malformed call therefore no longer writes a row and then throws an uncoded TypeError, and a retry cannot duplicate the row. null still means absent. The DoD sanitizer, the placeholder and the empty-DoD warning are unchanged. docs/MCP_SERVER.md's create_task section gains an Input refusals paragraph.
acceptanceCriteria: DoD 'Tests pass', '["a","b"]', {a:1} and ['ok',1] are each refused INVALID_INPUT naming the field. No task file is written and no TASK_CREATED is logged, and a valid retry creates exactly one row.

taskRails that is not an array, holds a non-string or empty entry, has more than 100 entries, or has an entry longer than MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS is refused INVALID_INPUT, and the exact boundary values are accepted.
Valid input is stored as given. null on either field acts as absent. DoD [] and [''] keep the placeholder and its warning.
The existing createTask, createCommitActor, epicDeleteActor and getContext tests stay green.
invariants: Every refusal happens before state.createTask, so it writes nothing.
The dodCount warning reads the caller's validated list, never the stored placeholder.
compatibility: null and absent definitionOfDone or taskRails behave as before.
DoD contents are still sanitized by taskStore (empty entries dropped, 50 items, 1000 chars), and the placeholder warning is unchanged.
The schemas already advertise both fields as string arrays.

docs/MCP_SERVER.md: one Input refusals paragraph in ### moe.create_task
reuse: validateStringArrayValue and MAX_EPIC_RAIL_CHARS (state/validators.ts:250-275) are the validator create_epic uses for epicRails at :584.
The repro cases come from /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/A/zzHuntA_createTaskDodShape.test.ts and zzHuntA_createTaskRails.test.ts.

state/taskStore.ts:315-317 sanitizes the DoD to the placeholder, :327 stores `input.taskRails.slice(0, 100)` raw, and :307 refuses an ARCHIVED epic.

state/validators.ts:252 validateStringArrayValue(value, field, maxItems, maxItemLength, truncate): it rejects a non-array, an over-count list, a non-string `field[i]` and an empty `field[i]`, plus an over-long entry when truncate is false.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Use validateStringArrayValue for definitionOfDone too. Rejected: it refuses empty entries and more than 50 items, which today's sanitizer silently accepts, and it would break the documented placeholder warning for [] and ['']. (2) Put the checks in taskStore.createTask so /ws CREATE_TASK is covered as well. Rejected: no plugin sends either field, and that file belongs to the held-back order and status items. (3) Compute dodCount from the stored task, as the row's fix hint says. Rejected: the stored placeholder hides the empty-DoD warning.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: create_task's guardrails are advisory by design, but caller-shape errors (epicId, title, status, priority, dependsOn) already throw before the write. This extends that existing pre-write band. McpAdapter does not enforce inputSchema, so handler checks are the only gate.
planningNotes.risks: A client that sends taskRails with more than 100 entries or with empty strings is now refused instead of silently trimmed. 0 of 897 live rows have a bad entry. The doc paragraph names the bounds.
